description:
Advances: ancora.findings, ancora.gate

Wave 2 of ancora-gg8, after the drift-split ticket (both edit the registry statements; sequential keeps the counts honest). A1 + A2 in the investigation record; findings-A and the architecture decision are comments on the epic. Both codes are disclosures: info tier, diff-scoped, blocking nothing — they make the two invisible self-reports (a borrowed tag, a rewritten statement) visible at the only moment anyone has context to judge them.

Deliverable:
A. tags/tag_borrowed (info, diff-scoped): fires when a diff ADDS a `@tag spec:` naming a requirement id that pre-exists the diff and whose statement lines are untouched in the same diff. Message names the tag site (file) and the requirement id, phrased as a review pointer ("new test binds to unchanged requirement X; confirm the test exercises it"). Inputs exist: base and head tag maps are both already scanned (lib/ancora/gate.ex:86-87); ChangeAnalysis already does diff-scoped set comparisons. Backfilling coverage is legitimate and encouraged — info is mandatory, not a compromise.
B. append/statement_changed (info, diff-scoped): keep the statement in AppendOnly's model (today it drops it — {id, subject_id, priority} only, lib/ancora/append_only.ex:105-130), compare normalized strings between base and HEAD, and emit one finding naming each requirement id whose statement text changed. This also makes the currently silent Ack trigger legible: the same spec edit that clears a subject's drift now shows up as a statement_changed line in the same run.
No judgment of the text change (narrowing vs widening) — that classification is not honestly computable and was declined on the epic.

Spec delta (land in this same diff):
- ancora.findings.registry_closed: count 31 -> 33 (base tip 134862f already reads 31 after gg8.5), add tags/tag_borrowed and append/statement_changed to the enumerated list.
- ancora.findings.registry_defaults: add info defaults for both.
- ancora.gate.diff_scoped_versus_repo_state: add both codes to the diff-scoped list.
- ancora.gate.two_append_guards: append the amendment sentence — "The diff-scoped disclosure `append/statement_changed` (info) is not a guard: it names requirement ids whose statement text changed and never blocks or authorizes anything; the guard set remains exactly the two above." (This is the slimmed_governance amendment; ancora.decision.field_friction_response records it.)
- ancora.gate: new requirement ancora.gate.borrowed_tag_disclosed (must) for A's semantics, and ancora.gate.statement_change_disclosed (must) for B's, each with scenarios: (A1) new tag on pre-existing unchanged requirement -> tags/tag_borrowed info naming both ends; (A2) new tag on a requirement whose statement is edited in the same diff -> no tag_borrowed; (A3) new requirement + new tag in same diff -> no tag_borrowed; (B1) statement reworded -> append/statement_changed info naming the id; (B2) whitespace-only reformat -> nothing; (B3) priority-only change -> no statement_changed (must_downgraded already covers it).

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for every scenario above; existing append-guard suite untouched and green; registry closure test updated to 33.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: all six scenarios; the drift-ack interplay — a spec edit that acknowledges drift produces both the :ack-marked drift finding (from the previous ticket) and the statement_changed line in one run.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe tmp-repo fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: both disclosures live on existing gate paths (ChangeAnalysis for tags, AppendOnly for statements); proving tests are the gate fixture scenarios.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/output*.ex (summary grammar landed in the previous ticket; new codes flow through existing formatting)
- lib/ancora/trailer.ex
- lib/ancora/config.ex

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/finding.ex (registry entries)
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex
- lib/ancora/append_only.ex
- lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex (only if tag-site line info needs surfacing)
- test/**
- docs/migration.md and priv/spec_init/agents/SKILL.md.eex (registry enumeration: the two new codes and count; pre-authorized by orchestrator 2026-09-04T00:33Z because the scaffold doc and template tests enumerate every registry code)
- .spec/README.md (registry count line 31 → 33; pre-authorized 2026-09-04T01:34Z)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (only the ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 call site and the threading of base_tags to it; ruling 2026-09-04T01:42Z)
- lib/ancora/review.ex and .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (only if the review renderer or its tests need to classify the two new codes; substantive spec sentence plus decisions: link if drift fires; pre-authorized 2026-09-04T00:33Z)
- .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (the statement edits and scenarios above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No severity above info for either code, ever, in defaults
- No semantic classification of statement changes; no footprint-overlap scoring; no in-gate mutation (all declined on the epic)
- No spec.review binding-table affordance (declined; revisit only if reviewers keep rebuilding it by hand)

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Findings:
[WARNING] ancora.derive derived/growth - :: ancora.derive: tests now call new functions: Ancora.ChangeAnalysis.findings/6 — acknowledge them in the spec for this subject
[WARNING] ancora.derive derived/shrink - :: ancora.derive: tests stopped calling Ancora.ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 — drop the dead contract from the spec or restore the coverage
[WARNING] - change/missing_decision .spec/README.md :: governance file .spec/README.md changed without a decision update; add or update an ADR in the same diff

spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=0 warnings=3

The targeted touched-file tier passed 65 tests, and mix test --stale passed 365 tests and 3 properties before spec.check failed.

RULING: keep ChangeAnalysis.findings at arity 5; gate.ex call site is in scope; one README trailer authorized; the two red runs do not count

All three warnings dissolve under this ruling, so neither red final-tier run counts against the cap; you have two fresh capped runs. Your uncommitted work stays.

1. derived/growth and derived/shrink on ancora.derive come from your arity change: ancora.derive's tests reach Gate.check, which now calls a new ChangeAnalysis.findings/6 and no longer calls findings/5. Do not change the public arity. Keep `findings/5`; make the fifth argument a single map, `%{head: head_tag_map, base: base_tag_map}` (derive the old `tagged_ids` inside as `Map.keys(head_tag_map)`), or another shape of your choice that keeps arity 5. Update the callers and tests accordingly. No growth/shrink trailer.
2. `lib/ancora/gate.ex` is in Allowed touches for exactly that call site and the threading of `base_tags` into it (the hunks you already have), nothing else. The ticket description now lists it.
3. change/missing_decision on `.spec/README.md` (the registry count line, a frontmatter-less governance file) is by design the co-change rule. Because the change is a mechanical count bump with no contract change, your commit may carry exactly one trailer: `Spec-Ack: change/missing_decision=info`, with a commit-body line "README registry count 31 → 33; mechanical, no contract change." Confirm the edited specs still link ancora.decision.field_friction_response in decisions: so nothing else needs that trailer. No other Spec-Ack code.
4. Then re-run the change-scoped final tier with `mix spec.check --base 134862f53b00cfe7be62977286ebf8a19f9b8537`, prove each new assertion against its mutation in a scratch copy as before, commit referencing ancora-gg8.6, and record IMPLEMENTED with the same session tag (gg8.6-impl-1) and log path.
This consumes no attempt.

RULING: two trailers are authorized; drop the compatibility clause; the two red runs do not count

The drift on ancora.derive for ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 is transitive: ancora.derive's tests reach Gate.check, which calls the changed function, and the function's own subject (ancora.gate) is substantively edited in your diff. That is the standing wave-2 rule in your rule pack ("Transitive drift"), and my README ruling's "no other Spec-Ack code" sentence wrongly overrode it. Corrected:

1. Your commit may carry exactly two trailers:
   `Spec-Ack: change/missing_decision=info` (body line: "README registry count 31 → 33; mechanical, no contract change.")
   `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info` (body line: "Transitive drift only: ancora.derive reaches ChangeAnalysis.findings/5; its own subject ancora.gate is substantively edited in this diff (B2 fan-out).")
   No other code. Do not edit ancora.derive.spec.md.
2. Remove the base-compatible list clause of findings/5: it is dead code kept to dodge a hash, and drift fires on the changed body regardless. Keep one clause taking the tag-map argument (arity 5), update callers and tests.
3. Both red runs were red solely on this finding, so neither counts; you have two fresh capped runs. Amend or add to commit a2e2276 (the trailers go on the commit whose diff they explain; amending is fine since nothing has been merged), re-run the change-scoped final tier with `mix spec.check --base 134862f53b00cfe7be62977286ebf8a19f9b8537`, and record IMPLEMENTED with the same session tag (gg8.6-impl-1) and log path. If a different finding appears, post WORKER_ERROR quoting it and stop.
This consumes no attempt.
